newsitem.title: CANADA: Sands Petroleum buys into Arakis. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sands Petroleum buys into Arakis. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]

text.p: Sands Petroleum AB, a Swedish company affiliated with Canada's International Petroleum Corp (IPC), has amassed about seven percent of Arakis Energy Corp's stock and is lobbying to install a director on Arakis's board.

But Sands and IPC, two of several international companies controlled by the Lundin family, have no plans "in the near future" to launch a bid for all of Arakis's stock, IPC director Lukas Lundin said in a telephone interview from Vancouver.
"We hold 7.2 million shares. We filed with the SEC," Lundin said. "There will be a press release tomorrow, I guess."
The purchase was being viewed by the acquisitor as an investment and not immediately as a way of establishing a toehold for a takeover bid, he said.
"Not in the near future -- that's not our plan at all," he said. "We met with management on Sunday and told them this was a friendly deal as long as they give us a board seat."
Takeover speculation regarding Arakis intensified over the past week as large volumes of the company's shares changed hands in Nasdaq trade.

Arakis, which is developing a 12.2-million-acre oil concession in strife-torn Sudan, fueled the speculation on Friday by saying it was vulnerable to a takeover and was instituting a shareholder rights plan.

IPC lobbied unsuccessfully last year for a stake in Arakis's US$1 billion joint venture to develop its project. It recently won operatorship of less-explored concession in Sudan adjacent to the Arakis lands.
The Arakis investment "is very cheap. It has big reserves. It's one of the biggest basins in the world and they control lots of it," Lundin said.
Arakis's partners in the project are China National Petroleum Corp, Malaysia state oil company Petronas and the Sudan government. Petronas and Sudan also have interests in the IPC concession.
Lundin said Arakis officials were expected to respond to the board seat request later this week.
Meanwhile, Arakis said on Monday it appointed former Occidental Petroleum Corp and Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd executive James B. Taylor to its board.
Other board members would be proposed for shareholder approval at Arakis's next annual meeting, it said.

Arakis also said it formed an advisory committee to assist directors in decisions regarding the company's expanded Sudan operations and in other international ventures. The committee's membership was expected to be announced shortly.
